definition: Perceptual refers to processes involved in noticing and telling apart sensory information, such as distinguishing between visually similar stimuli. In this packet, it especially concerns implicit, automatic learning that improves later discrimination after exposure.

reasons: The packet supports perceptual learning, not the general adjective/perceptual sense defined here; the requested sense is therefore mismatched.
“Processes involved in noticing and telling apart sensory information” is an unsupported broad generalization beyond the packet’s discussion of one experimental perceptual-learning paradigm.
The packet supports implicit, automatic learning that affects later discrimination, but not the definition’s framing of “perceptual” itself as that process.

The first sentence gives a general definition of “perceptual” as “processes involved in noticing and telling apart sensory information,” but the packet does not provide an explicit general definition of “perceptual”; it discusses “perceptual learning” and discrimination in a specific task context.

The second sentence’s restriction (“In this packet, it especially concerns implicit, automatic learning that improves later discrimination after exposure”) is supported, but the definition contains an additional broader claim not evidenced by the packet.
